items.title: Memory chip crunch could last 2 more years, JPMorgan says
items.summary: Yahoo Finance Senior Business Reporter Ines Ferre joins Opening Bid to discuss JPMorgan's (JPM) latest note, warning that the memory chip shortage could continue for at least two more years. Ferre also breaks down the S&P 500's (^GSPC) bullish run, which has produced 26 record closes in 2026.

items.title: Micron Stock Rises Despite Reported Apple Supplier Threat
items.summary: Apple's reported testing of Chinese memory chips introduces another competitive variable as Micron's AI revenue reaches record levels.

items.title: Coherent (COHR) Stock Is Tumbling Today After Massive Optics vs. Memory Debate on Social Media This Weekend
items.summary: A weekend debate on social media about optics replacing memory as the hottest AI trade sent optical stocks surging at Monday's open, then something unexpected happened within the first ten minutes of trading.

items.title: Apple, Sionna, AbCellera, Sandisk, SpaceX, Berkshire,  and More Stocks That Explain Today’s Market
items.summary: Apple  fell 2% to $306.56.  Jefferies downgraded shares to Underperform from Hold and slashed the price target to $263.66 from $285.56.  Shares of Elon Musk’s rocket and artificial-intelligence company snapped a four-week losing run on Friday with a 16% surge following the end of a lockup period for shares.

items.title: The Next Breakout For This Tech Stock Could Be Hiding in Plain Sight
items.summary: SanDisk surged nearly 2,900% in a year before a sudden 30% pullback rattled investors, but the real question is whether that drop signals danger or sets up the next major move.

items.title: These Stocks Could Be Ready for Their Next Big Move
items.summary: Micron, Super Micro, and Dell are sitting at the center of the AI infrastructure buildout, but whether each name has enough fuel left for another major run in 2027 depends on a very different set of catalysts and risks for each one.

items.title: Why Micron is Decisively Better Positioned Than Intel Now
items.summary: Both Micron and Intel just reported earnings that crushed expectations, but one company is locking in guaranteed billion-dollar AI contracts while the other is still waiting for its first external foundry customer to sign.
